slides.title: Scarcity and choice
slides.notes: Name what scarcity means and give one opportunity cost from daily life. Notes: a farmer can grow 40 tonnes of wheat or 20 of maize on one field; learners say what giving up one tonne of wheat costs in maize.

slides.title: Demand and supply
slides.notes: Explain why price changes move buyers and sellers in opposite directions. Notes: draw a demand line and a supply line for a market stall, then shift one at a time and say what happens to price and quantity.

slides.title: Equilibrium and elasticity
slides.notes: Calculate equilibrium and price elasticity of demand from simple equations. Notes: demand Q = 100 minus 2P and supply Q = 20 plus 2P give price 20 and quantity 60; raising price to 22 cuts quantity by about 6.7 per cent, elasticity about minus 0.67.

slides.title: Growth, inflation and the multiplier
slides.slide: L4 Practitioner · Growth, inflation and the multiplier
slides.notes: Apply the multiplier and measure inflation from index numbers. Notes: an index rising from 200 to 210 is 5 per cent inflation; a marginal propensity to consume of 0.8 gives a multiplier of 5, so an injection of 10 raises income by 50.

slides.title: Market failure and policy
slides.slide: L5 Specialist · Market failure and policy
slides.notes: Analyse an externality and compare a tax, a subsidy and regulation. Notes: with a marginal external cost of 4 per unit and 1,000 units sold, a tax of 4 raises 4,000; learners list who gains, who loses and one unintended effect.

slides.title: Market power and welfare
slides.slide: L6 Advanced · Market power and welfare
slides.notes: Derive monopoly output and deadweight loss and compare with competition. Notes: demand P = 100 minus Q with marginal cost 20 gives monopoly output 40 at price 60 and profit 1,600; competition gives 80, so the welfare loss is 800.

slides.title: Growth models and causal evidence
slides.slide: L7 Super expert · Growth models and causal evidence
slides.notes: Evaluate a growth model and the identification strategy behind a policy claim. Notes: with saving rate 0.2, depreciation plus population growth 0.05 and capital share 0.5, steady-state capital per worker is 16; discuss what instrument would justify a causal reading.
